lines: A three-row step sequencer with a control voltage knob and a gate button on every step, an internal clock, and a clock divider for each row
Sets the voltage this row's CV output carries while this step is the active one, 0-10V
Switches this step's gate on or off for this row; the lamp beside it is lit while it is on
Sets how many clocks this row takes before moving on a step: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 16, 32, 48 or 64, shown on the display beside it
Sets how many steps the sequence runs before it starts again, 0 to 8; at 0 the module stops and the step lamps go out
Sets the rate of the internal clock, one pulse a second at the bottom of its travel down to one every 0.05 seconds at the top; it does nothing while a cable is in the external clock jack
Switches the gate outputs between Continuous, which holds 10V for as long as that step is the active one, and Trigger, which is a 1ms pulse of 10V as the step arrives
The clock the sequencer runs on; every change from 0V to any other voltage counts as a clock, and patching this jack takes the speed knob out of use
Any change from 0V to another voltage here puts every row back to its first step; clocks arriving in the moment after that are ignored
Passes on the clock the sequencer is running on: the external clock when one is patched, and otherwise the internal clock as a 1ms pulse of 10V
The voltage of the CV knob at this row's active step, 0-10V
The gate of this row's active step, 10V or 0V; a 1ms pulse in Trigger mode and held for the whole step in Continuous mode
Note — with a Sequel Save placed immediately to the right, the whole panel can be saved to four slots and brought back by button or trigger
Note — the three rows share one clock but each has its own divider, so they drift apart and come back together, which is how the polyrhythms are made
Note — a row's CV output is only written while something is patched to it
Menu — Randomize all CV knobs — gives every CV knob on the panel a new random voltage
Menu — Randomize all gates — turns every gate button on the panel on or off at random
Menu — Randomize CV knobs for row 1 — gives the CV knobs of the top row new random voltages
Menu — Randomize Gates for row 1 — turns the gate buttons of the top row on or off at random
Menu — Randomize CV knobs for row 2 — gives the CV knobs of the middle row new random voltages
Menu — Randomize Gates for row 2 — turns the gate buttons of the middle row on or off at random
Menu — Randomize CV knobs for row 3 — gives the CV knobs of the bottom row new random voltages
Menu — Randomize Gates for row 3 — turns the gate buttons of the bottom row on or off at random
Menu — Sample and hold — holds each row's CV output at the voltage it had when that row last fired a gate, instead of following the active step
Menu — Use DD cable color scheme - Light — replaces Rack's cable colour list with five colours of the maker's, after a confirmation step; the item ends in Dark under the Rack dark-panel setting

lines: Turns typed text into a rhythm by spelling it out in Morse code, one clock to a unit of time
Sets how many units of time a dot lasts, 0 to 9
Sets how many units of time a dash lasts, 0 to 9
Sets how many units of silence separate one letter from the next, 0 to 9
Sets how many units of silence separate one word from the next, 0 to 9
Steps the sequence on by one unit; every change from 0V to any other voltage counts as a clock
Any change from 0V to another voltage here takes the sequence back to its first unit; clocks arriving in the moment after that are ignored
10V while the current unit is part of a dot or a dash and 0V while it is silence; it holds its value between clocks
A 1ms pulse of 10V each time the sequence returns to its first unit
Note — the module does nothing until there is both a clock and some text: click the large black screen and type, and click outside it to stop typing
Note — only the letters A to Z and the digits 0 to 9 are understood; anything else is left out
Note — the strip along the bottom shows how long the sequence has become
Note — international Morse code is used, and the four knobs come up at the standard lengths: a dot of 1, a dash of 3, 3 between letters and 7 between words
Note — one unit of time is the gap between two clocks, so a fast clock gives the most usable rhythms

lines: A polyphonic oscillator that bends the phase of its wave, with glide, an amplitude control, three modulation inputs, hard sync and a noise output
Sets the pitch, in semitones either side of middle C; in LFO mode the same knob is read as a power of two instead, reaching far below the audible range
Sets how long the pitch takes to slide from one note to the next; below about a fiftieth of its travel there is no slide at all, and it does nothing in LFO mode
Bends the phase of the wave, 0.02 to 0.98: on the sine and triangle it works towards a sawtooth, and on the square it works like pulse width
Sets how far the voltage at the BM jack moves the bend, from full inversion through nothing at the middle to full
Sets how far the voltage at the FM jack moves the frequency, from full inversion through nothing at the middle to full
Switches LFO mode on and off: the three wave outputs drop far below the audible range and swing 0-10V rather than either side of zero, and glide stops working
Sets the level of the three wave outputs, 0 to 1
Sets how far the voltage at the AM jack moves the level, from full inversion through nothing at the middle to full
Restarts the wave from the beginning whenever the voltage here crosses, which is hard sync; the square output of another oscillator is the usual thing to patch
Sets the pitch, 1V per octave added to the frequency knob, and its channel count is what sets the polyphony of the whole module
Moves the bend away from the knob setting, a fifth per volt scaled by the BM knob, and the total is held between 0.02 and 0.98
Moves the frequency away from the knob setting, scaled by the FM knob; it is added to the frequency itself rather than to the pitch, which is linear frequency modulation
Moves the level away from the knob setting, a fifth per volt scaled by the AM knob, and the total is held between 0 and 1
The square wave, ±5V, or 0-10V in LFO mode; it is drawn from a softened table in oscillator mode and a hard-edged one in LFO mode
The sine wave, ±5V, or 0-10V in LFO mode
The triangle wave, ±5V, or 0-10V in LFO mode
White noise, one channel for each channel of the oscillator
Note — the module is polyphonic and takes its channel count from the pitch input; with nothing patched there it runs one channel
Note — in LFO mode the three wave outputs stop swinging either side of zero and run from 0V upwards instead
Note — the frequency is held below half the sample rate, so heavy frequency modulation stops rather than folding back
